scope: Manual family reconciliation of the 738 non-drop selected review records from current two-profile primary-crate MIR, plus named source/dependency/profile supplements. This is Q3 producer classification, not Q4 aggregate admission or Q5 destructor/caller qualification.

boot_memory.contract: Mandatory BSP validation allocates one aligned 8192-byte scratch layout and tests one private frame; no runtime entry.

boot_lp.contract: Validated 1..256 LP factories, schedulers, AP stacks/tables, APIC-ID map and shootdown acknowledgements; boot lifetime, no hotplug. PerLp/boxed_slice concrete callers are fixed boot storage or inactive helpers.

boot_timer.contract: BSP preallocates queues and one timer Arc per validated LP; owning LP initializes hardware once before the barrier. Runtime get cannot construct storage.

boot_firmware.contract: BSP ACPI catalog has at most 8187 XSDT addresses; IORT has at most 4093 nodes and one cached immutable config. MCFG/PCI has 32 windows, 256 bus identities/window and global 16384 device/function limits.

boot_tags.contract: Hardware-width ASID return storage reserves 256 or 65536 u16 slots before user tag publication. Return cannot grow; original root/invalidation rules remain authoritative.

boot_log.contract: CPU vendor/model strings come from fixed 12/48-byte CPUID data; firmware diagnostic output is bounded by the catalog and emitted once by finish_boot. Unknown table signatures format borrowed bytes.

boot_ingress.contract: Compiled cluster configuration and encoding reject more than protocol MAX_SERVICES=16 before collection allocation. Temporary fixed-count bindings/encoded launch bytes are used by trusted boot composition only.

inactive.contract: ShardLocal, ShardMailboxSet, generic closure IPI, unused VecQueue, uncharged IdTable insertion/default snapshot helpers and MADT indexing have fixture-only or no callers. InterruptRoutingManager mutation is todo and its empty/default/clone bodies have no operational caller. New production use requires review.

deferred_stub.contract: DeferredTask is uninhabited and no worker/submission exists; pinned unbounded queue construction allocates no blocks. Adding a task variant or production caller requires bounded admission and progress review.

fixture_profiles.contract: Kernel S3/Kafka/Kafka-step profile-building helpers are called only by optional self-tests. Encoders validate protocol bounds; operational connector launch consumes the admitted encoded plaintext instead.

completion.contract: Completion records/nodes/accounts, CQ ring/backlog bytes and watch/observer references have separate existing admission and complete owners. Borrow/upgrade/return operations do not create another independent allocation charge.

ipc.contract: Namespace/payload/endpoint nodes, queue backing, staging/loan/descriptor/revocation/attachment vectors and returned work remain with captured exact-generation owners and independent byte/count reservations. Prepared capacity precedes publication/retirement.

capability.contract: Capability/account/node publication prepares backing against the exact unpublished/captured root; original class survives transfer, retirement and weak retention.

thread.contract: Thread node plus ThreadContext bytes are admitted together before allocation; stacks/root tables and waiter/timer accounts retain their own owners. Scheduler lookup/guard results borrow existing boot scheduler Boxes.

tables.contract: Runtime root/thread IdTables use charged candidates for payload/generation/return-ID arrays, including old/candidate overlap. Retirement reuses prepared capacity; uncharged generic insertion has no production caller.

iommu_ledger.contract: DMA ledger vectors reserve exact capacity through the containing table/domain owner and existing iommu_nodes backing; pushes do not grow published storage.

observer_timer.contract: Observer entries/handles/list/account backing and anonymous timer node/cancellation ownership use existing typed fallible admission. Reference/delivery transfers retain the original allocation owner.

shared_allocator.contract: ByteAllocator and ChargedAllocator are backend adapters, not new resource families. Concrete callers supply typed layout/class reservations; allocation holders retain admission through final weak/deallocation.

memory_objects.contract: Object frame catalogs and snapshots retain their existing prepared byte reservations and captured backing classification; actual frames keep physical admission. Bare default snapshot wrapper is fixture-only.

inputs.contract: Primitive image/descriptor/pickup/plaintext buffers capture actor class and retain byte admission through deallocation; sensitive spare capacity is wiped.

launch_cache.contract: Complete launch/handoff/upgrade parents retain source/target roots, profiles, transfers and admitted vector prefixes. Fixed image cache reserves independent bytes/count before I/O and immutable publication.

telemetry_q4.contract: Diagnostic snapshots/encoding use fallible prepared buffers and one 1 MiB per-request working bound. They still require aggregate and original-principal backing admission; per-request bounds are not accepted as that proof.

frame_tracking_q4.contract: Each heap/image frame reserves physical admission before fallible owned_frames tracking growth; registration pushes only into prepared capacity. Count follows admitted backing, but vector capacity/old-candidate overlap still needs original-principal/aggregate kernel-byte coverage.

source_supplements.disposition: Shared borrowed decoder/validator uses 3840-byte fixed list scratch and no heap, with a <=4096 compile-time fence; userspace-owned decode materializes vectors only after validation. No new credential-byte copy.
Borrowed fields and bounded encoded frame, no metadata vectors. Encoded plaintext/input remains in the accepted Q1 owner.

Current parsers borrow bounded input or use caller-provided output; digest and signature/AEAD work use fixed storage. Input/plaintext owners remain Q1/Q2. This does not establish secret erasure under forced abort or authenticated security time.

Bounded IPI queues allocate their slot backing at construction and do not grow on push/pop; uninhabited DWM has no submission. Once/locks and reference clones do not allocate backing. Preserve the earlier boot dependency review; new producers require review.

Existing pinned local C backend has six planned boot allocations and no write/parser allocations; checked geometry/12 MiB request bound and inert retained complete context remain. Full native display deadline incident stays unresolved.

Device-tree discovery is a stub and the optional ARM profile lacks working power/IOMMU integration; RISC-V is not an operational target. HVF omits protected DMA/PCI probes and is not production-isolation qualification. Test helpers are gated or have only fixture callers; compiled generic bodies are not reachability.

limitations: Dependencies, optional profiles and compiler/allocator internals require explicit review; their bodies are not supplied by a primary-crate MIR dump.
Collection operations can reuse prepared capacity; owned results can move existing storage; reference clones and empty constructors normally allocate no backing.
Drop records include harmless guard releases and generic operands. An explicit drop call value_type describes its result; the consumed type remains in callee.
The unstable MIR format and selected API patterns are not an exhaustive allocator/call-graph analysis. Missing source spans and opaque factories remain review obligations.

Family grouping records reviewed dispositions; the grouping script is not a safety or reachability proof. Generic callers, dependency internals, macro bodies and future features still require contributor-contract review.

The selected API census is supplemented by concrete source call searches, existing accepted owner contracts and named dependency/profile edges. It is not a claim that every possible future allocation has been mechanically discovered.
Required Q4 rows remain explicit work; no per-request or boot count bound proves aggregate/principal coverage. The omitted 2028 Drop candidates remain Q5 and are not accepted by this review.
